title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and configurable timeouts
author: Jenna Park
release_notes: Tune continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce head-of-line blocking, add fairness weights across priority queues, protect against starvation, and introduce per-request queueing timeouts with safe fallbacks. Observability and config defaults added. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: observed intermittent high tail latencies under mixed workloads where long-generation requests starved short requests behind them in the continuous batching layer. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and add configurable per-request queue timeouts so long-wait requests are either scheduled more fairly or evicted to fallback paths. High level changes: 1) introduce per-queue fairness weights and a simple deficit-based scheduler to ensure small/low-cost requests get allocation proportional to configured weights; 2) add starvation detection heuristics that temporarily boost priority for queues with long-waiting items; 3) configurable queueing_timeouts (default 2s for interactive profiles, 10s for long-run profiles) with graceful eviction that can route the request to a lower-cost model variant or return a structured retry hint; 4) integration with KV cache eviction to avoid cache thrash when timeouts trigger preemption; 5) new metrics and tracing spans for queue wait distributions, boost events, timeout evictions, and per-queue throughput; 6) feature-flag gated rollout with canary percentage and runtime-config mapping per model/profile. Compatibility: fully backward-compatible on the public API. The scheduler behavior is behind a runtime feature flag and controlled by per-deployment config. Tests and validation: unit tests for scheduler invariants, microbenchmarks against perf-canary scenarios, canary rollout on internal staging with a 5% traffic slice, and end-to-end validation using the eval-harness prompt set for mixed short/long generation mixes. Related: ENG-2741 queueing fairness research notes, ENG-2805 KV-cache interactions with preemption. Checklist: - [x] design doc + perf plan attached to Linear ENG-2741 - [x] unit tests for deficit scheduler and starvation boost - [x] integration tests for timeout eviction and fallback routing - [x] perf microbenchmarks show 45-70% reduction in 99th percentile latency for short requests under mixed load - [x] added observability (metrics, traces, dashboard links) - [x] feature-flagged + rollout plan - [x] change log / release notes prepared Notable decisions: we chose a deficit-based scheduling approach because it is lightweight and composes well with the existing continuous-batcher batching window logic. Starvation boosts are transient and decayed to avoid oscillation. Timeouts are a safety mechanism not a primary scheduling control; default timeouts were tuned conservatively to avoid premature evictions. Migration and rollout: default feature flag off; ramp to 100% after 2 weeks of canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and monitoring thresholds for error increases and model-quality regressions. If regressions detected, automatic rollback path included.

review_conversation: Carlos Mendoza (reviewer): Overall design looks sound. Two concerns: (1) how do we guarantee boosts don't create priority inversion under pathological bursts? (2) need a clearer signal for metrics that will drive automatic rollback decisions.

Jenna Park (author): For (1) boosts decay over a short sliding window (configurable) and we added an anti-oscillation backoff. I'll add comments and a unit test that simulates pathological bursts. For (2) added dedicated metrics: boost_events_total, boost_duration_seconds, timeout_evictions_total and a rollout health check spec in the docs.
Aisha Gupta (reviewer): Please ensure KV cache hooks are low overhead. Also suggest adding an opt-in config for experimental models to skip timeout eviction so long-running evals don't get evicted.

Jenna Park (author): cache_integration uses lock-free hints and only updates hot-key counters; added skip_eviction_profiles list and added microbenchmarks showing <1% overhead in p99 throughput in steady state.
Evan Li (approver): Verified perf numbers on canary 5% slice. Observed 65% reduction in short-request p99 under mixed load. Approving to merge once CI passes and docs link is included.
